discussion_comments.comment_body: This still strikes me as fragile. Why don't we look at the whole value and use an existing function like [`isStringImplicitContextValue`](https://github.com/myselfsiddharth/vscode/blob/7a5872ab8274dd67636bb69563ac9f237b4ae5c3/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/attachments/chatVariableEntries.ts#L884).
What if we add some other kind in the future that also has an undefined handle?

targetHandle !== undefined is really standing in for "this came from isStringImplicitContextValue," which is fragile exactly like you said: a future kind with no handle would silently be misclassified.

The check already happens at the one call site that builds the target, in implicitContextAttachment.ts

const stringValue = isStringImplicitContextValue(context.value) ? context.value : undefined;
Rather than re-deriving "is this string-shaped" inside the matcher from a single field, I'll thread that result through explicitly as part of IImplicitContextAttachmentTarget (e.g. an isStringTarget: boolean, set from stringValue !== undefined), and have isImplicitContextAlreadyAttached read that flag instead of inferring it from handle. That way the type check happens once, where the real value is in scope, and the matcher never has to guess from a proxy field.

Does that address it, or would you rather the matcher take the raw context.value itself and call isStringImplicitContextValue internally? Slight tradeoff: that couples the matcher to the value union type instead of keeping IImplicitContextAttachmentTarget a flat DTO 

happy to go either way.

> Rather than re-deriving "is this string-shaped" inside the matcher from a single field, I'll thread that result through explicitly as part of IImplicitContextAttachmentTarget (e.g. an isStringTarget: boolean, set from stringValue !== undefined), and have isImplicitContextAlreadyAttached read that flag instead of inferring it from handle. That way the type check happens once, where the real value is in scope, and the matcher never has to guess from a proxy field.

This seems good to me, thank you.
I find this pretty confusing. A string context value actually does have a `resourceUri`, but here we are saying it does not.
If we need to check if it's a string implicit context, then we should be explicit about that.

Good catch. I extracted the narrowed string context value into a single local so that both `handle` and `resourceUri` clearly come from the same value rather than separate inline checks.

Fixed in `3709bb9`.

The fourth tuple element (color) was typed as ThemeColor (non-optional) before this PR — the | undefined was introduced by mistake and has been reverted. Only the fifth element (backgroundColor) is new and intentionally typed as ThemeColor | undefined since it is an optional field in vscode.FileDecoration.

Regarding the broader suggestion to make the first three elements (propagate, tooltip, badge) also | undefined: these predate this PR and their types are an existing design choice. The <DecorationData> cast on the sender side already handles actual optionality without type errors, and the consumer already guards bubble with ?? false. Changing those elements would be an unrelated refactor that belongs in a separate PR.

Fair point — color can totally be undefined, a decoration might only set backgroundColor. The main thread code already handles it with themeColor?.id optional chaining, the type just wasn't reflecting that. Will fix the tuple.

The identity key is now built three different ways:
- The host omits a falsy `directSourceId`, including `''` (`copilotRuntimePluginEnablement.ts`).
- This function uses `?? null`, so `''` and `null` produce different keys.
- `mergeCopilotSessionAndInstalledPlugins` uses `JSON.stringify` with a raw `undefined`.

A shared helper in `common/meta/runtimePluginEnablement.ts` that normalizes with `|| null` would remove the drift. The discovery tests also don't cover a direct-source plugin yet.
